shuowen:4001.text: The fief of Yandi’s descendants of the Jiang surname, and the state of Zhou Qi’s maternal family: Tai County, 斄, in Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 台 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “He established his household at Tai.”

shuowen:4002.text: King Wen of Zhou’s fief, in Zhongshui Township, Meiyang, Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4003.text: King Tai of Zhou’s state, in Meiyang, Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4004.text: A county in Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 眉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4005.text: Yuyi, 郁夷, in Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 有 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4006.text: A county name in Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 雩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4007.text: The fief of a clan sharing the Xia rulers’ surname, which fought at Gan. In Hu, 鄠, are Hu Valley and Gan Pavilion. Formed from 邑, with 戶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4008.text: A township in Hu, Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 崩 indicating the sound. Chengfu in Pei also has a 䣙 Township. Read like 陪.

shuowen:4009.text: A township in Hu, Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4010.text: A township in Hu and Zhouzhi, Right Fufeng. Formed from 邑, with 赤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4011.text: King Wen of Zhou’s capital, southwest of Duling, Jingzhao. Formed from 邑, with 豐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4012.text: A county in Jingzhao, the fief of You, son of King Li of Zhou. Formed from 邑, with 奠 indicating the sound. When Zongzhou fell, Zheng moved to the Zhen and Wei rivers; this is the present Xinzheng.

shuowen:4013.text: Heyang County, 郃陽, in Left Fengyi. Formed from 邑, with 合 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “On the sunny side of the He.”

shuowen:4014.text: A township in Lantian, Jingzhao. Formed from 邑, with 口 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4015.text: A township in Duling, Jingzhao. Formed from 邑, with 樊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4016.text: A county in Left Fengyi. Formed from 邑, with 麃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4017.text: 䣝陽 Pavilion in Left Fengyi. Formed from 邑, with 屠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4018.text: A place in Gaoling, Left Fengyi. Formed from 邑, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4019.text: A township in Gukou, Left Fengyi. Formed from 邑, with 秊 indicating the sound. Read like 寕.

shuowen:4020.text: Shanggui, 上邽, in Longxi. Formed from 邑, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4021.text: Dibu, 狄部, in Tianshui. Formed from 邑, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4022.text: A granary site in Hongnong County. Formed from 邑, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4023.text: A place on an official road directly facing the city gate in Henan County. Formed from 邑, with 辱 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “King Cheng established the tripods at Jiaru, 郟鄏.”

shuowen:4024.text: A Zhou settlement. Formed from 邑, with 輦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4025.text: A Zhou settlement. Formed from 邑, with 祭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4026.text: A settlement on Mount Mang north of Luoyang, Henan. Formed from 邑, with 亡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4027.text: A Zhou settlement. Formed from 邑, with 尋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4028.text: A Zhou settlement in Henei. Formed from 邑, with 希 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4029.text: A township in Qinshui, Henei. Formed from 邑, with 軍 indicating the sound. Lu also has a place called 鄆.

shuowen:4030.text: An old Shang settlement, the area north from Chaoge in Henei. Formed from 邑, with 北 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4031.text: The fief of a son of King Wu of Zhou, in Yewang, Henei. Formed from 邑, with 于 indicating the sound. Also read like 區.

shuowen:4032.text: A feudal state under Yin, northeast of Shangdang. Formed from 邑, with 𥝢 indicating the sound; 𥝢 is ancient-script 利. The Book of Shang says: “The Earl of the West subdued 𨛫.”

shuowen:4033.text: A Jin settlement. Formed from 邑, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4034.text: A Jin settlement. Formed from 邑, with 冥 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Attack Ming’s three gates.”

shuowen:4035.text: A settlement of Jin’s Marquis of Xing. Formed from 邑, with 畜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4036.text: A place in Wen, Jin. Formed from 邑, with 侯 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Dispute over the fields of 𨜫.”

shuowen:4037.text: A Jin settlement. Formed from 邑, with 必 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Jin and Chu fought at Bi.”

shuowen:4038.text: The settlement of Shuhu, a grand officer of Jin. Formed from 邑, with 谷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4039.text: A place in Wenxi County, Hedong. Formed from 邑, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4040.text: A village in Wenxi, Hedong. Formed from 邑, with 虔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4041.text: A township in Wenxi, Hedong. Formed from 邑, with 匡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4042.text: A place in Linfen, Hedong, where the Han sacrifices to Sovereign Earth. Formed from 邑, with 癸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4043.text: The fief of a son of the Duke of Zhou, near Huai in Henei. Formed from 邑, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4044.text: A county in Taiyuan. Formed from 邑, with 烏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4045.text: A county in Taiyuan. Formed from 邑, with 示 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4046.text: A county in Wei Commandery. Formed from 邑, with 業 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4047.text: 𨙷 Pavilion in Zheng territory. Formed from 邑, with 井 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4048.text: Handan County, 邯鄲, in Zhao. Formed from 邑, with 甘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4049.text: Handan County, 邯鄲. Formed from 邑, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4050.text: A state enfeoffed to a son of King Wu of Zhou, in Jin territory. Formed from 邑, with 旬 indicating the sound. Read like 泓.

shuowen:4051.text: A county in Qinghe. Formed from 邑, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4052.text: A county in Changshan, where Emperor Shizu (Guangwu of Han) took the throne; now called Gaoyi. Formed from 邑, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4053.text: A county in Julu. Formed from 邑, with 梟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4054.text: A county in Zhuo Commandery. Formed from 邑, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4055.text: Yuzhi County, 郁郅, in Beidi. Formed from 邑, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4056.text: A northern state of the Tall Di, called the Fangfeng clan under Xia and the Wangmang clan under Yin. Formed from 邑, with 叜 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The 𨜛 Man invaded Qi.”

shuowen:4057.text: The fief of the Marquis of Fu, descended from Yandi’s Taiyue, in Yingchuan. Formed from 邑, with 無 indicating the sound. Read like 許.

shuowen:4058.text: A county in Yingchuan. Formed from 邑, with 亢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4059.text: A county in Yingchuan. Formed from 邑, with 匽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4060.text: A county in Yingchuan. Formed from 邑, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4061.text: Xinqi, 新郪, a county in Runan. Formed from 邑, with 妻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4062.text: A state of the Ji surname north of the Huai; now Xinxi, 新鄎, in Runan. Formed from 邑, with 息 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4063.text: A neighborhood in Shaoling, Runan. Formed from 邑, with 自 indicating the sound. Read like 奚.

shuowen:4064.text: A pavilion in Tongyang, Runan. Formed from 邑, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4065.text: A Cai settlement. Formed from 邑, with 狊 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The daughter of the boundary officer of Juyang fled to him.”

shuowen:4066.text: A state of the Man surname, now belonging to Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4067.text: A place in Deng state. Formed from 邑, with 憂 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The people of You, on Deng’s southern border, attacked them.”

shuowen:4068.text: A township in Yuyang, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 号 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4069.text: A township in Zaoyang, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 巢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4070.text: The present Rang County in Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4071.text: A township in Rang, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4072.text: A pavilion in Xi’e, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 里 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4073.text: A pavilion in Wuyin, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 羽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4074.text: Chu’s former capital, ten li north of Jiangling in Nan Commandery. Formed from 邑, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4075.text: A county in Nan Commandery, renamed Yicheng in Xiaohui’s third year. Formed from 邑, with 焉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4076.text: A county in Jiangxia. Formed from 邑, with 𪓑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4077.text: A township in Yin, Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 葛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4078.text: A county in Jiangxia. Formed from 邑, with 㖾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4079.text: A county in Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 己 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4080.text: A county in Jiangxia. Formed from 邑, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4081.text: A state south of the Han. Formed from 邑, with 員 indicating the sound. Hanzhong has Yun Pass, 鄖關.

shuowen:4082.text: A state of the southern Yi. Formed from 邑, with 庸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4083.text: A county in Shu. Formed from 邑, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4084.text: A place in Jiangyuan, Shu. Formed from 邑, with 壽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4085.text: A place in Shu. Formed from 邑, with 耤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4086.text: A township in Guanghan, Shu. Formed from 邑, with 蔓 indicating the sound. Read like 蔓.

shuowen:4087.text: Shifang, 什邡, a county in Guanghan. Formed from 邑, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4088.text: 存䣕, a county in Jianwei. Formed from 邑, with 馬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4089.text: A county in Zangke, 䍧牱. Formed from 邑, with 敝 indicating the sound. Read like 鷩 in 鷩雉.

shuowen:4090.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4091.text: A state of the western Yi. Formed from 邑, with 冄 indicating the sound. Anding has Chaona County, 朝𨙻.

shuowen:4092.text: Poyang, 鄱陽, a county in Yuzhang. Formed from 邑, with 番 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4093.text: A county in Changsha. Formed from 邑, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4094.text: A county in Guiyang. Formed from 邑, with 林 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4095.text: The present 䣂陽 County in Guiyang. Formed from 邑, with 耒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4096.text: A county in Kuaiji. Formed from 邑, with 貿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4097.text: A county in Kuaiji. Formed from 邑, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4098.text: Pei Commandery. Formed from 邑, with 巿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4099.text: A lower settlement of Song. Formed from 邑, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4100.text: A county in Pei state. Formed from 邑, with 虘 indicating the sound.
